title: Biological continued pretraining: data sources and token budgets
timestamp_policy: Human-facing generation time is fixed PST (UTC-8). The directory date is the UTC research date.
scope: Biological continued pretraining, including corpus-curation experiments, with explicitly separated from-scratch comparisons. Non-CPT methods and reusable corpora are supporting references; clinical-model references are archived outside the main review.
method: Targeted web searches, citation following, and reading primary papers, official technical reports, and author repositories. This is a broad targeted review, not an exhaustive systematic census or a common-protocol model leaderboard. Unknown details remain unknown.
execution: Literature review and small source snapshots only. No new OCR, model inference, training, paid teacher generation, GPU allocation, or bulk paper collection. Existing experiments and scores are unchanged.
interpretation_rules: Corpus tokens, training tokens consumed, distinct papers, abstracts, packed sequences, and image-caption pairs are different units. Counts across models overlap and must not be added.
PMC-derived does not establish whether a model used XML, PDFs, or an upstream extraction. A missing OCR description is not evidence that OCR was never used upstream.

Continued pretraining (CPT) means additional language-model training on a domain corpus. Instruction tuning (SFT) means training on task prompts and target responses. Older papers sometimes call both fine-tuning.
A teacher's educational-quality score is a curation signal, not scientific truth or independently adjudicated extraction ground truth.
Published benchmark numbers below are author-reported and protocol-specific. They are not measurements from our 50-paper extraction experiment.
Clinical evidence ranking and exclusion of animal studies should not be copied into a corpus intended for biological research.

notes: BioMatrix's scientific text uses FineFineWeb biology/chemistry/medicine/health and literature; its figure also names bioRxiv. No numeric paper/web split is supplied. Figure 3 subdivides protein tokens into **36.0B sequence / 38.5B structure / 2.9B other**; molecule tokens into **32.1B sequence / 17.6B structure / 24.0B other**; cross-entity tokens into **17.1B sequence / 11.4B structure / 19.5B other**. The “other” subdivisions should not be relabeled entirely as generated text. Sources include PubChem, UniRef/UniProt, PDB/AFDB, interaction datasets and GPT-generated MolTextNet descriptions; exact individual budgets remain NR. These modalities are biomolecular representations, not paper-figure pixels. [BioMatrix, Figure 3 and §3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.22138v1#page=12)

**BioMatrix:** Continues Qwen3 on 304.4B tokens spanning literature/web text, PubChem records, protein sequences and structures, interactions and interleaved text/entities. It includes GPT-generated MolTextNet descriptions and computational structures as well as experimental PDB structures. Its TrEMBL branch explicitly removes literature citations and evidence codes. These provenance differences should remain visible in a scientific corpus. [§3.1–3.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.22138v1)

The existing-dataset lower bound was corrected from 25.6B to 176.7B after checking all Figure 3 categories against the source descriptions in §3.1.2–3.1.4. This changes the review’s allocation, not the paper’s reported total.

dimensions.clarity: Extensive method and limitation sections help; broad single-model framing is stronger than what the task-group results establish.

catalog_policy: One source record per model/study/corpus. The public overview merges CPT models and CPT data-curation studies, names the initialization and selects one sourced budget per entry. Full budgets and prior evidence remain in the same registry.

migration.import_scope: Public paper/model metadata and links only; no benchmark cases, labels, prompts or raw evaluation outputs copied.

categories.online_papers: Direct acquisition from publication repositories/publishers, including paper/abstract PDF, XML, LaTeX and bibliographic-text exports.
categories.web_urls: Direct acquisition/processing of non-paper webpages, including raw archived webpage responses.
categories.existing_datasets: Already assembled external corpora or datasets, including paper/web corpora and structured biological databases. Reused article text is not counted again as direct papers.

token_budget_policy.unknown: NR is not zero. No word/document/example count is substituted for tokenizer tokens. Available counts and consumed/sampled/scheduled counts are separate.
token_budget_policy.partial: Lower bounds contain only identified source components. Residual totals are not assigned to unknown categories.
token_budget_policy.scope: Route is assessed at the reviewed acquisition/curation pipeline, not merely the final model loading a corpus file. Source-specific token definitions remain explicit.
token_budget_policy.evidence: Numeric values retain primary source URLs and sections; new category sums record their arithmetic. Raw fetched primary sources and hashes are in the ignored audit directory.

presentation_policy.overview: One selected budget per model/study; count label distinguishes retained corpus, training exposure and positions.
presentation_policy.initialization: Existing checkpoints for CPT; random weights for from-scratch comparisons. Architecture alone does not establish initialization.
presentation_policy.excluded: Instruction-only, representation-only, general-purpose and clinical-only models do not appear in the CPT overview.
presentation_policy.evaluation: Separate private repository; do not copy benchmark cases, labels or raw evaluation outputs into the extraction literature review.
presentation_policy.content_scope: Acquisition route and biological content are separate axes. General replay, other science, clinical literature and non-text tokens must be explicit. A mixed headline is never a biology-only token estimate.

evidence_assessment_policy.scope: Qualitative source-based judgment of evidence for training/data claims; not author prestige, publication venue, model parameter count or independent replication.

levels.stronger_controls: More direct comparisons/ablations of the claimed training intervention.
levels.useful_limited: Informative reported evidence with important remaining confounds or disclosure gaps.
levels.limited: Major limitations on interpreting the central claim, such as unresolved contamination or mismatched evaluation framing.

evidence_assessment_policy.institution_display: Compact first-author/group credit and shortened institutions in the overview; reviewed-source names on study pages.

overall_paper_assessment_policy.purpose: Overall quality and value of the whole paper in its publication context, separate from project relevance and narrow evidence-strength labels.

labels.solid: Worthwhile and broadly credible work with meaningful limitations.
labels.mixed: Substantial strengths and weaknesses constrain the overall case.

overall_paper_assessment_policy.status: Provisional editorial judgment; not an official reviewer rating, venue ranking or independent replication.

modality_policy: Acquisition route and representation are orthogonal. Modality counts are included in source budgets and must never be added on top. Distinguish pure modality-token counts, domain buckets with mixed representations, and later-stage encoder features.
overview_sort: Within CPT and from-scratch sections: Strong, Solid, Mixed, Weak; alphabetical within each rating.
